response:
Diagnosis: gen 4 produced a decisive result. Replacing the one-year capex growth rate with the firm's five-year own-history position in capex intensity (TS_RANK(capx/ppent, 5)) while keeping the industry-adjusted labor-productivity conditioner improved every metric at once — FMB -5.38, FF5 alpha -5.4%/yr with t=-5.22, Sharpe -0.519, coverage 0.119. So the mechanism is an investment *state* at a multi-year peak, not an annual change, and the intangible conditioner that matters most is organizational productivity (revenue per employee), which also repaired the previously FMB-null goodwill family (Goodwill_Overhang_Unproductive_Operator: FMB -2.40, alpha -6.7%, t=-4.17, Sharpe -0.49). Note also that broadening the investment leg with acquisitions at level scale (Total_Hard_Expansion_Unproductive) *hurt* alpha (-1.2%, t=-1.34), so acquisition flows do not belong in the same additive leg as capex intensity; goodwill stock is the better acquisition-side state variable. This generation consolidates: (i) fuse the two winning states, (ii) test the intensity denominator and the dual conditioner against the new leg, (iii) finally test the R&D-based conditioner with the repaired investment leg (the core tangible-versus-knowledge comparison), (iv) rebuild the long side around productivity, and (v) open recognized intangible *formation* flows, which have never been tested (only levels, which failed).

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Peak_Capex_Goodwill_Unproductive
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5), SUMRANK(RATIO(gdwl, sale), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(sale, emp)))))
HYPOTHESIS: The worst investment state combines both routes to hard-asset expansion — a five-year peak in internal capital spending and a large stock of previously acquired goodwill — in a firm that lacks the organizational productivity to earn a return on either.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The two strongest archive signals share the productivity conditioner but differ in the expansion state (peak capex intensity, alpha -5.4%; goodwill overhang, alpha -6.7%), and those states are only weakly overlapping, so fusing them should compound the short-leg alpha rather than dilute it. Unlike gen-4's failed capx-plus-aqc leg, this keeps acquisition exposure as a balance-sheet stock (goodwill) rather than a lumpy annual flow, which is why it should add information instead of noise.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Capex_Per_Revenue_Peak_Unproductive
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, sale), 5), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(sale, emp))))
HYPOTHESIS: Capital spending at a five-year high relative to revenue — rather than relative to installed plant — is the sharper statement that capacity is being added ahead of demand, and it is most damaging for firms with low organizational productivity.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This isolates one design choice against the front-runner: the scaling denominator of investment intensity, revenue (a demand measure) versus net plant (a capital-stock measure). Because both variables are broadly reported the test runs at full coverage, and the answer tells us whether the mechanism is overcapacity relative to the market or over-replacement of existing assets.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Peak_Capex_Dual_Moat_Deficit
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5), SUMRANK(NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(sale, emp))), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Peak-intensity physical expansion is most punished in firms deficient in both intangible advantages — process efficiency and pricing power — since they can neither operate new capacity well nor price its output.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: With the one-year growth leg, adding the margin conditioner to the productivity conditioner improved alpha from -2.9% to -3.2% and t from -3.35 to -3.51, so the two moat proxies carry partly independent information; pairing them with the much stronger TS_RANK investment state is the natural consolidation at full coverage. If alpha does not improve over Signal 1's family, we learn that productivity alone spans the intangible-quality dimension and can simplify the final signal.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Peak_Capex_Knowledge_Starved
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5), NEG(RATIO(xrd, sale)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms at a multi-year peak of physical investment while spending little on research are substituting bricks for knowledge, and this tangible-tilted allocation of the investment budget predicts low returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This is the direct tangible-versus-knowledge comparison at the heart of the task, and it repairs gen-0's failed indicator-based version (alpha -0.2%, t=-0.21) by replacing the discarded-half conditional and the noisy one-year growth leg with the proven continuous R&D-intensity rank and the five-year investment state. Comparing it to the productivity-conditioned version tells us whether the intangible ingredient that matters is realized organizational output or reported research spending, with coverage restricted to R&D reporters as the known cost.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Productive_Research_Capex_Restraint
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(sale, emp)), SUMRANK(RATIO(xrd, sale), NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: The mirror of the overexpansion anomaly is a highly productive, research-intensive firm that is deliberately restraining physical capital spending relative to its own history; its value creation is expensed and its capital discipline is unrewarded in accounting profitability.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every reliable archive result is short-side driven, and the long-side channels (cash-buffered innovation, funded capital-light innovator) delivered ~3% alphas with t>3 but zero FMB slope, indicating a poorly graded cross-section; importing the two ingredients that created gradient on the short side — industry-adjusted productivity and the five-year investment state — should give the long side a monotone slope as well. This is a substantive reconstruction rather than a variant, because it replaces the liquidity leg with a productivity leg on the theory that unrecognized intangible capital shows up as output per worker.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Identifiable_Intangible_Formation_vs_Plant
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5), NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(intan, gdwl), 1), sale)))
HYPOTHESIS: Investment directed into identifiable intangibles — patents, technology, licenses, customer relationships, excluding goodwill — reflects capability building with durable rents, whereas peak-intensity plant spending reflects commodity capacity; firms tilting toward plant and away from intangible formation underperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The archive has tested recognized intangible *levels* (which failed, FMB -0.06) but never recognized intangible *formation flows*, which are the true investment-side analogue of capex and are available for far more firms than R&D. Netting goodwill out of the change in intangibles removes acquisition premiums, so the leg measures purchased capability rather than deal accounting, making this a genuinely new comparison within the investment budget.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
